command: benchmark/hg002/run_wholegenome.sh per individual VCF (HG001/2/3/4); totals in benchmark/giab_cohort_rescue (run_cohort.sh)
data_provenance: FOUR real GIAB benchmark individuals (HG001/NA12878, HG002/NA24385, HG003/NA24149, HG004/NA24143), v4.2.1 biallelic SNVs, whole-genome chr1-22, GRCh38 + GENCODE v49. Per individual+chromosome: bcftools SNV-consensus haplotype, scan every annotation intron for reference bias (non-canonical on the linear reference, canonical on the individual's haplotype = CREATED), adjudicate the variant axis (wgs provenance for the rescue, unknown for the firewall). Annotation+variant scan; no RNA-seq/caller runs. No private data.
notes: COHORT-level yield of the reference-bias rescue across four personalized human genomes (extends the single-sample HG002 result). Each individual carries 31-37 genuine reference-bias splice junctions (137 total); the variant axis rescues ALL of them (137/137, 100% sensitivity), with 0 false rescues, and the circularity firewall holds every one (137/137) under circular-risk provenance. So the rescue is a consistent, perfectly-specific guardrail across individuals -- a few dozen false-novel calls exonerated per personalized genome -- not a one-off. Its practical value rises with sample divergence from the linear reference.
